questions.q: What is the key difference between a filter and a prompt in an OTBI analysis?
options: There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A filter is a fixed condition baked into the analysis; a prompt lets the person running it supply a value at run time
Filters only work in Table view; prompts only work in Graph view
Prompts can only be used in BI Publisher, never in OTBI
questions.explain: Filters apply the same condition every time for every user; prompts let each run (or each viewer) supply a different value.

questions.q: Which condition is a good candidate for a permanent filter rather than a prompt?
options: The business unit a regional AP lead wants to see
Payment Status = Unpaid, for an analysis meant to always show only open invoices
The date range a viewer wants to analyze this week
The dollar threshold a user wants to test today
questions.explain: A condition that should never change for any viewer, like restricting to unpaid invoices, is a good fit for a fixed filter rather than a prompt.

questions.q: Why would a consultant add a Business Unit prompt to a shared analysis instead of building ten separate analyses, one per region?
options: Prompts are required by Oracle for all analyses
A single prompted analysis lets each regional AP lead see only their own region's data without duplicating the analysis design ten times
Prompts make an analysis run slower, which is desirable
Filters cannot be combined with prompts in the same analysis
questions.explain: A prompt reuses one analysis design across many viewers, each supplying their own value, avoiding unnecessary duplication.

questions.q: Which OTBI view type is best described as "closest to a raw export, with every selected column as plain rows"?
options: Graph
Pivot Table
Table
Dashboard
questions.explain: Table view presents selected columns as plain rows, good for detail-level review, as opposed to the aggregation of Pivot Table or the visual summary of Graph.

questions.q: Can a single OTBI analysis include more than one view, such as a table and a graph?
options: No, each analysis is limited to exactly one view
Yes — multiple views can be added to the same analysis and switched between, built from the same underlying column selection
Only if the analysis is first converted to a BI Publisher report
Only administrators can add more than one view
questions.explain: A common pattern pairs a detail table for drill-down with a graph for an at-a-glance summary, both built from the same column selection.
